title: Candidate Concierge: Orchestration Runbook for High-Velocity Hiring
body:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook defines the "Candidate Concierge" orchestration pattern: a lightweight People Ops-led workflow that coordinates sourcing, interviewing, hiring decisions, and day-0 onboarding for high-velocity roles (IC eng, infra, early core product hires). The goal is to improve candidate experience SLA, reduce time-to-offer, and maintain consistent calibration across interviewers while keeping an auditable trail for compliance.

When to use this runbook:
- Roles expected to convert in <= 21 days from first contact (volume hiring windows, urgent backfills, growth-market campus cohorts)
- Hiring tracks where a single People Ops coordinator can manage a 1:6 recruiter-to-candidate ratio

Core principles:
1) Concierge ownership: one named People Ops coordinator owns end-to-end orchestration for each candidate (scheduling, pre-interview brief, feedback consolidation, offer logistics, day-0 checklist).
2) Async-first communications: push templates and reminders by email/Slack; reserve live syncs only for calibration or offer escalation.
3) Lightweight evidence model: each interviewer submits a 3-line summary + rubric score within 24 hours; coordinators prevent stale feedback.
4) Candidate empathy: internal SLAs for response windows and transparent timeline updates.

Intake and role definition (first 48 hours):
- Intake form fields (quick): role name, band/IC level, hiring manager, expected start window, must-have skills, nice-to-have skills, hiring committee members, target interview timeline (days), compensation band link. (Form: GitHub gist / Confluence template CON-4827)
- Triage decision: Recruiter + Hiring Manager + People Ops 15-min sync to confirm timeline and identify two backup interviewers.

Sourcing cadence and outreach:
- Sourced candidate SLA: initial outreach -> response window 3 business days. If no response, second follow-up at day 4 then archive.
notes: This document is intentionally framed as a compact runbook for operational use. It contains templates and a reproducible rubric for interviewer calibration. Keep confidential candidate/compensation data out of Drive; store in HRIS.
